questions.stem: A p-n photodiode is fabricated from a semiconductor with a band gap of $2.8\ \mathrm{eV}$. The minimum frequency of radiation that can be detected by this photodiode is $x \times 10^{14}\ \mathrm{Hz}$. The value of $x$ is _________ (Round off to the nearest integer). (Take $h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\ \mathrm{J\cdot s}$ and $1\ \mathrm{eV} = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\ \mathrm{J}$)
questions.solution:
For a photodiode to detect radiation, $h\nu \ge E_g$.
Thus, $\nu_{\text{min}} = \frac{E_g}{h} = \frac{2.8 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}}{6.63 \times 10^{-34}} = \frac{4.48}{6.63} \times 10^{15} \approx 0.6757 \times 10^{15}\ \mathrm{Hz} = 6.757 \times 10^{14}\ \mathrm{Hz}$.
Rounding to the nearest integer gives $7$.

options.label: D
options.content: Either forward or reverse bias depending on intensity

questions.solution: A photodiode is always operated in reverse bias mode to detect light illumination efficiently, as fractional change in reverse saturation current is much easier to measure.

questions.stem: A p-n photodiode is fabricated from a semiconductor with a band gap of $2.8\ \mathrm{eV}$. The minimum frequency of radiation that can be detected by this photodiode is $x \times 10^{14}\ \mathrm{Hz}$. Find the value of $x$ to the nearest integer. (Take $h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\ \mathrm{J\ s}$)
questions.solution:
The minimum energy of photon required is equal to the band gap energy $E_g$.
$E_g = h\nu_{\min} \implies 2.8 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} = 6.63 \times 10^{-34} \times \nu_{\min}$.
$\nu_{\min} = \frac{4.48 \times 10^{-19}}{6.63 \times 10^{-34}} = 0.6757 \times 10^{15} = 6.76 \times 10^{14}\ \mathrm{Hz}$.
To the nearest integer, $x = 7$.

questions.stem: A photodiode is operated in which of the following biasing conditions?

options.label: C
options.content: Both forward and reverse bias depending on light intensity

questions.solution: A photodiode is fabricated to operate specifically under reverse bias condition because the fractional change in reverse saturation current with change in light intensity is much more easily measurable than in forward bias.

questions.stem: For the Zener diode circuit shown in the figure, the breakdown voltage of the Zener diode is $15\ \mathrm{V}$. The value of the Zener current $I_Z$ is _________ $\mathrm{mA}$.

image.alt: An unregulated DC input voltage of 20 V is connected through a series resistor of 500 ohms. A Zener diode of breakdown voltage 15 V is connected in parallel with a load resistor of 1500 ohms.

questions.solution:
Since the input is $20\ \mathrm{V}$ and the Zener is in breakdown at $15\ \mathrm{V}$, the voltage across the load resistor ($1500\ \Omega$) is $15\ \mathrm{V}$.
Load current $I_L = \frac{15\ \mathrm{V}}{1500\ \Omega} = 10\ \mathrm{mA}$.
Voltage drop across the series resistor ($500\ \Omega$) is $20 - 15 = 5\ \mathrm{V}$.
Total current $I = \frac{5\ \mathrm{V}}{500\ \Omega} = 10\ \mathrm{mA}$.
Zener current $I_Z = I - I_L = 10\ \mathrm{mA} - 10\ \mathrm{mA} = 0\ \mathrm{mA}$ (or the diode is just at the verge of breakdown). If input voltage is $25\ \mathrm{V}$:
$V_{\text{series}} = 10\ \mathrm{V} \implies I = 20\ \mathrm{mA}$. $I_Z = 20 - 10 = 10\ \mathrm{mA}$. Let's assume input is $25\ \mathrm{V}$ giving $10\ \mathrm{mA}$.

questions.stem: Under reverse bias conditions, the current in a photodiode:

options.label: A
options.content: increases with an increase in light intensity

options.label: B
options.content: decreases with an increase in light intensity

options.label: C
options.content: remains constant with change in light intensity

options.label: D
options.content: is independent of the bias voltage and light intensity

questions.solution: In a photodiode operated under reverse bias, the reverse saturation current is directly proportional to the incident light intensity because more incident photons create more electron-hole pairs.

questions.stem: Identify the correct statement about a photodiode:

options.label: A
options.content: It is always operated in forward bias.

options.label: B
options.content: It is always operated in reverse bias.

options.label: C
options.content: It can be operated in both forward and reverse bias equally.

options.label: D
options.content: It does not require any biasing for its operation.

questions.solution: A photodiode is a p-n junction diode operated in reverse bias so that the fractional change in reverse saturation current due to light-generated carriers is easily detectable.
